newsitem.title: USA: Newmont mulls fate of Santa Fe gold hedges.
newsitem.headline: Newmont mulls fate of Santa Fe gold hedges.

text.p: Newmont Mining Co has no immediate plans to alter its hedging strategy in light of its recent takeover of Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp, Chief Financial Officer Wayne Murdy.
"At this point in time we have taken the view that we are not hedging," Murdy said. "We have not determined how we are going to deal with the (Santa Fe's) portfolio."
In March, Newmont, one of the world's biggest gold producers, acquired Santa Fe in a deal worth $2.5 billion.
Newmont is almost entirely unhedged regarding its own production, while the vast majority of Santa Fe's output is hedged through the next 18 months, equivalent to 1.5 million ounces, Murdy said.
He spoke to reporters at a Goldman Sachs and Co commodities conference here.
"We have not made any final decision as to whether we are going to close it out or let it roll out," Murdy said in reply to how Newmont would integrate Santa Fe's hedged production.
Asked if he was concerned the German Bundesbank might sell some of its gold reserves, Murdy commented:"I wish they would hold on to their assets."

German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said Thursday that the central bank's gold reserves should be revalued to put them closer to the market level but stressed that there would be no sales of Bundesbank gold.
Murdy also said Newmont continued to be bullish on gold prices despite the recent weakness.
"The fundamentals are very strong," Murdy said. "There is a lot of uncertainty about the European currency, but there are a lot of shorts in the market right now."
